text:
Oliver: Quick sync re: rate-control refactor. thinking split admission out to policy svc? tradeoffs?

Maria: Router-local wins on latency and burst handling. Policy service gives central rules and global fairness but adds rpc latency + coupling. :thinking:

Chen: If external, router needs a hot cache + async refresh. local token-cache with fast expiry seems right.

Ben: Remote policy increases failure modes. router needs graceful defaults; consider a tiny embedded fallback engine.

Carla: Product needs per-tenant quotas, per-route SLAs, and abuse spike scoring. How do you expose? simple admit API or full DSL?

Oliver: API sketch:
```
POST /admit
{ "tenant_id": "t-123", "route": "/generate", "tokens": 125, "priority": "normal" }
=> { "allow": true, "reason": "ok", "lease_ms": 50 }
```
router uses lease_ms to shape bursts.

Maria: Lease model good. Also add backpressure hint: recommended_delay_ms when near budget.

Chen: Abuse signals: short-term token rate + short blacklists. Policy svc can own rules but router must run high-confidence heuristics per request.

Ben: Migration: 1) policy API read-only (router caches) 2) dual-write config UI 3) consult remote with local overrides 4) full cutover. Keep observability tight.

infra-bot: deploy: Canary of router-with-cache at staging-3 scheduled for 2029-03-12T09:00Z :eyes:

Oliver: Add decision latency, cache hit rate, denies-by-policy vs denies-by-quota, fairness-score metrics.

Maria: Keep v1 schema minimal: tenant_id, route, tokens, priority, sample_tags. DSL later.

Chen: Perf note: gRPC + batching between router and policy svc. implement circuit-breaker: if remote latency > X, fall back to local soft-quotas and alert.

Carla: Action items: Oliver+Chen prototype cache/lease; Ben write migration doc; Maria collect product knobs; infra schedule canary + SLOs.

Oliver: I'll post RFC followup with seq diagrams and small API spec. Thanks :thumbsup:
